Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was A LOT of paper work and bureaucracy, were I had to fill out papers, some of the same once, both for my own university, Charles University, and the EU - it seemed a bit exaggerated

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The course registration at Charles University is quite stressing, and as a Master student, I do not understand why master student do not get prefered inMaster classes, as they are the only classes I could get credit for in Copenhagen

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: check the courses and have a long list of courses you want to take, as it is quite stressful when you have to register, and you have to be very very quick if you want one of the popular courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: the level of courses were lower than what I am used to, and I do not understand how Bachelor and Master students can take the same courses, as our academic levels are different

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Copenhagen - as I am not to fond of to much discussion in class and giving your own opinion - for me, that was what I did in high school not at university. Further, I feel like the classes in Copenhagen are better prepared as there are more formal and strict rules they have to follow where at Charles at seemed a bit ad hoc and what the professor felt for in the moment. However, there were some of the professors at Charles that were very passionated - but I found it weird that there was not a larger focus on method and proper research.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Grand Debates of European Integration, Small States in the EU, Great Geopolitical Powers: Russia, Economic Transformations of post-Soviet States, The Transformation of post Communist parties

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Great Geopolitical Powers: Russia - It gave insights into the Russia culture and political system that I could not have gained at home
